```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(bmm)
library(brms)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidybayes)
source(here::here("_common.R"))
dat_simple <- read.csv(here::here("data", "m3_simple_span.csv"))
dat_simple$ss_fac <- factor(dat_simple$ss_fac, levels = c(2, 4, 6, 8))
fit_simple <- readRDS(here::here("models", "m3_simple.rds"))
```



## Resources: workshop materials {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}
Scan the QR code to open the workshop materials.

Open `examples/02_m3.qmd` for data, code, pre-fitted models, and checks.

In this session, we will:

- Identify the **activation sources** supporting each response.
- Translate activation into choice probabilities using **softmax and option counts**.
- Estimate **item and binding memory** with bmm.
- Extend the model to examine **distractor filtering**.

:::

::: {.column .m3-choice-formulas width="55%"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=0}

$$
P(\mathrm{old})=
\frac{b+a}{(b+a)+b}
$$

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}

$$
P(\mathrm{new})=
\frac{b}{(b+a)+b}
$$

:::

:::

::: {.column .m3-choice-formulas width="55%"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=0}

$$
P(\mathrm{old})=
\frac{\exp(b+a)}{\exp(b+a)+\exp(b)}
$$

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}

$$
P(\mathrm{new})=
\frac{\exp(b)}{\exp(b+a)+\exp(b)}
$$

:::

## Concept: item activation and choice {#stronger-item-memory-favors-the-old-image .m3-figure}

```{r}
#| label: recognition-demo
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "Illustrative softmax probabilities: old and new are equally likely when memory activation is zero; greater memory activation favors old."
recognition_demo <- expand_grid(a = c(0, 1, 2), option = c("Old", "New")) |>
  mutate(b = 1, activation = b + if_else(option == "Old", a, 0),
         weight = exp(activation)) |>
  mutate(probability = weight / sum(weight), .by = a)
recognition_demo |>
  ggplot(aes(option, probability, fill = option)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", probability)), vjust = -0.4, size = 6) +
  facet_wrap(~a, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Old", "New")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(New = wk_colors[["grey"]], Old = wk_colors[["blue"]]), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Choice probability") + theme_workshop() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 20))
```

::: {.m3-binding-formula .fragment fragment-index=6}

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(\mathrm{correct}) &= b + a + c \\
A(\mathrm{other}) &= b + a \\
A(\mathrm{new}) &= b
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

## Concept: binding activation and choice {#what-does-binding-add .m3-figure}

```{r}
#| label: binding-demo
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "Illustrative predictions holding item activation fixed: correct and other are equally likely without binding; adding binding increases correct choices."
binding_demo <- expand_grid(c = c(0, 1, 2), option = c("Correct", "Others", "New")) |>
  mutate(option = factor(option, levels = c("Correct", "Others", "New")),
         b = 1, a = 1,
         activation = b + if_else(option == "New", 0, a) + if_else(option == "Correct", c, 0),
         weight = exp(activation)) |>
  mutate(probability = weight / sum(weight), .by = c)
binding_demo |>
  ggplot(aes(option, probability, fill = option)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~c, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Correct = wk_colors[["orange"]], Others = wk_colors[["blue"]], New = wk_colors[["grey"]]), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Choice probability") + theme_workshop() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 20))
```

A(\mathrm{Others}) &= b + a && \times 5 \\
A(\mathrm{NPL}) &= b && \times 4

$$

## Data: aggregating trial responses {#preparing-simple-span-data .m3-model-slide}

::: {.m3-preparation-content}

```{.r}
simple_span <- trials |>
  summarise(corr = sum(response_type == "correct"),
            other = sum(response_type == "other"),
            npl = sum(response_type == "npl"),
            .by = c(id, exp, setsize, n_corr, n_other, n_npl))
```

```{.text}
          id     exp setsize n_corr n_other n_npl corr other npl

2 10_openset openset       2      1       1     0   23     0   0

```

## Specify: the simple-span model {#specify-categories-and-their-option-counts .smaller .m3-model-slide auto-animate=true}

::::: {.m3-model-content}

```{r}
#| label: model-simple
#| code-line-numbers: "1-7|2|3|4|5|6"
model_simple <- m3(
  resp_cats = c("corr", "other", "npl"),
  num_options = c("n_corr", "n_other", "n_npl"),
  version = "ss",
  choice_rule = "softmax",
  links = list(a = "identity", c = "identity")
)
```

```{=html}
<script>
document.querySelector('#specify-categories-and-their-option-counts .sourceCode code').setAttribute('data-fragment-index', '0');
</script>
```

:::: {.m3-model-explanations}

::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=0}
`resp_cats`: observed response counts for Correct, Others, and NPL.
:::

::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=1}
`num_options`: available options in the same category order.
:::

::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=2}
`version`: `"ss"` = simple span · `"cs"` = complex span · `"custom"` = custom model.

:::

::: {.m3-choice-stage .fragment .current-visible fragment-index=3}
`choice_rule`: `"simple"` = Luce’s choice rule · `"softmax"` = exponential choice weights.

:::: {.columns .m3-choice-comparison}
::: {.column .m3-choice-panel}
::: {.m3-choice-equation}
$$
P(k)=\frac{n_k A_k}{\sum_j n_j A_j}
$$
:::
:::
::: {.column .m3-choice-panel}
::: {.m3-choice-equation}
$$
P(k)=\frac{n_k\exp(A_k)}{\sum_j n_j\exp(A_j)}
$$
:::
:::
::::

:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
`links`: map regression predictors to parameter values.

```{=html}
<div class="m3-link-headings"><h3 class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="7"><span class="fragment" data-fragment-index="4">identity</span></h3><h3 class="fragment" data-fragment-index="7"><span class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="9">log</span></h3><h3 class="fragment" data-fragment-index="9">logit</h3></div>
```

:::: {.columns .m3-link-layout}
::: {.column}
:::: {.m3-link-stages}
:::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=7}
::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
```{r}
#| label: link-identity
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "Identity inverse link: parameter value equals the regression predictor, including negative values."
link_predictors <- tibble(eta = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 201))
ggplot(link_predictors, aes(eta, eta)) +
  geom_line(color = wk_colors[["blue"]], linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Link scale", y = "Original scale") + theme_workshop()
```

:::
::::
:::: {.fragment fragment-index=7}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=9}
```{r}
#| label: link-log
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "Log inverse link: exponentiating the regression predictor produces positive parameter values."
ggplot(link_predictors, aes(eta, exp(eta))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = wk_colors[["grey"]], linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(color = wk_colors[["blue"]], linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 21)) +
  labs(x = "Link scale", y = "Original scale") + theme_workshop()
```

:::
::::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=9}
```{r}
#| label: link-logit
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "Logit inverse link: a logistic curve maps the regression predictor to parameter values between zero and one."
ggplot(link_predictors, aes(eta, plogis(eta))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, 1), color = wk_colors[["grey"]], linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(color = wk_colors[["blue"]], linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Link scale", y = "Original scale") + theme_workshop()
```

:::
::::

:::
::: {.column .m3-prior-distribution}
:::: {.m3-prior-sequence}
:::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=7}
::::: {.m3-prior-display}
:::: {.m3-prior-stages}
::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=5}

```{r}
#| label: prior-identity-link-distribution
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "The link-scale prior is Normal with mean 3 and standard deviation 1."
identity_prior <- tibble(value = seq(-1, 7, length.out = 401),
                         density = dnorm(value, 3, 1))
identity_distribution <- ggplot(identity_prior, aes(value, density)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = "Link scale"), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Link scale" = wk_colors[["blue"]],
                                "Original scale" = wk_colors[["orange"]])) +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Density", color = NULL) +
  theme_workshop() + theme(legend.position = "none")
identity_distribution
```

:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=6}

```{r}
#| label: prior-identity-both-distributions
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "The original-scale prior coincides with the link-scale prior under the identity link."
identity_distribution +
  geom_line(aes(color = "Original scale"), linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.7)
```

:::
::::

```{=html}
<div class="m3-prior-legend"><div class="m3-prior-link fragment" data-fragment-index="5">Link scale</div><div class="m3-prior-original fragment" data-fragment-index="6">Original scale</div></div>
```

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=7}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=9}
::::: {.m3-prior-display}
:::: {.m3-prior-stages}
::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=7}

```{r}
#| label: prior-log-link-distribution
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "The link-scale prior is Normal with mean 1 and standard deviation 0.5."
log_prior <- tibble(value = seq(-1, 10, length.out = 1001)) |>
  mutate(link_density = dnorm(value, 1, 0.5),
         original_density = dlnorm(value, 1, 0.5))
log_distribution <- ggplot(log_prior, aes(value)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = link_density, color = "Link scale"), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Link scale" = wk_colors[["blue"]],
                                "Original scale" = wk_colors[["orange"]])) +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Density", color = NULL) +
  theme_workshop() + theme(legend.position = "none")
log_distribution
```

:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=8}

```{r}
#| label: prior-log-both-distributions
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "The original-scale prior becomes a right-skewed lognormal distribution under the log link."
log_distribution +
  geom_line(aes(y = original_density, color = "Original scale"),
            linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.7)
```

:::
::::

```{=html}
<div class="m3-prior-legend"><div class="m3-prior-link fragment" data-fragment-index="7">Link scale</div><div class="m3-prior-original fragment" data-fragment-index="8">Original scale</div></div>
```
:::::

:::
::::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=9}
::::: {.m3-prior-display}
:::: {.m3-prior-stages}
::: {.fragment .current-visible fragment-index=9}

```{r}
#| label: prior-logit-link-distribution
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "The link-scale prior follows a standard normal distribution."
logit_prior <- tibble(value = seq(-8, 10, length.out = 1001),
                      density = dnorm(value, mean = 0, sd = 1))
logit_original <- tibble(value = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 999)) |>
  mutate(density = dnorm(qlogis(value), mean = 0, sd = 1) /
           (value * (1 - value)))
logit_distribution <- ggplot(logit_prior, aes(value, density)) +
  geom_line(color = wk_colors[["blue"]], linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.8)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Density") + theme_workshop()
logit_distribution
```

:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=10}

```{r}
#| label: prior-logit-both-distributions
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "The inverse logit transforms the standard normal prior into a distribution on zero to one."
logit_distribution +
  geom_line(data = logit_original, aes(value, density),
            color = wk_colors[["orange"]], linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.7)
```

:::

## Specify: parameter formulas {#specify-how-do-a-and-c-vary .smaller}

```{r}
#| label: formula-simple
#| code-line-numbers: true
formula_simple <- bmf(
  c ~ 0 + ss_fac + (0 + ss_fac | id),
  a ~ 0 + ss_fac + (0 + ss_fac | id)
)
```

::: {.incremental}
- `0 + ss_fac`: a separate mean for each **set size**.
- `(0 + ss_fac | id)`: correlated participant deviations at each set size.
:::

## Fit: the simple-span model {#fit-once-load-the-result-for-the-workshop .smaller .m3-model-slide}

::::: {.m3-model-content}

```{r}
#| label: fit-simple-settings
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
fit_simple <- bmm(
  formula = formula_simple,
  model = model_simple,
  data = dat_simple,
  prior = priors_softmax,
  chains = 4, cores = 4,
  iter = 5000, warmup = 2000,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
  sample_prior = "yes",
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  seed = 2026
)
```

The sampling arguments work the same way as in the SDT model.

:::::

## Evaluate: observed and predicted responses {#evaluate-does-m3-reproduce-the-responses .smaller .m3-figure}

`posterior_epred(fit_simple)` predicts counts in **all three categories**. Predictions match the observed proportions for correct responses and both error types.

```{r}
#| label: predictive-check
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "Observed and predicted open-set response proportions, with participant-level standard errors, across three categories."
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("data", "figures", "m3_simple_predictive.png"))
```

## Evaluate: item and binding estimates {#interpret-item-memory-and-binding-memory .smaller .m3-figure}

```{r}
#| label: posterior-plot
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-alt: "Open-set item and binding memory medians and 95 percent credible intervals across set sizes, in blue and orange facets on a 0 to 6 activation scale."
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("data", "figures", "m3_simple_parameters.png"))
```

- Item memory tends to decline with set size, but the estimates are uncertain.
- Binding memory declines clearly with set size.

:::

::: {.m3-binding-formula .m3-category-activations .fragment fragment-index=5}

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(\mathrm{correct}) &= b + a + c \\
A(\mathrm{paired\ distractor}) &= b + f a + f c \\
A(\mathrm{other\ targets}) &= b + a \\
A(\mathrm{other\ distractors}) &= b + f a \\
A(\mathrm{NPL}) &= b
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::::

## Specify: the complex-span model {#extend-the-model-keep-the-workflow .smaller}

```{r}
#| eval: false
model_complex <- m3(
  resp_cats = c("corr", "distc", "other", "disto", "npl"),
  num_options = c("n_corr", "n_distc", "n_other", "n_disto", "n_npl"),
  version = "cs", choice_rule = "softmax"
)

formula_complex <- bmf(
  c ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
  a ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
  f ~ 1 + (1 | participant)
)
```

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  const colors = {a: '#0028a5', c: '#dc6800', f: '#28a745', b: '#7f7f7f'};
  document.querySelectorAll('math mi:not([mathvariant="normal"])').forEach(symbol => {

  });
